title: Add automatic decryption for F5 tcpdump --f5 ssl captures
description:
# Summary

This change enables automatic decryption of BIG-IP `tcpdump --f5 ssl` captures by using the existing Wireshark secrets infrastructure.

BIG-IP `tcpdump --f5 ssl` captures contain TLS session secrets inside the F5 DPT trailer. Today, users must manually extract the keylog information and configure it separately in order to decrypt TLS traffic.

This change performs a lightweight prescan when an F5 capture is detected, extracts TLS secrets from the DPT trailer, and injects them into the existing secrets API before normal packet dissection starts.

As a result, F5 captures are decrypted automatically while non-F5 captures remain unaffected.

## Characteristics

* No preferences required.
* No temporary files.
* No Lua scripts.
* No pcapng conversion.
* No changes to the TLS dissector.
* No impact on non-F5 captures.
* Supports TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.
* Existing F5 Ethernet Trailer keylog fields remain available.

## Testing

Successfully tested with:

* F5 BIG-IP `tcpdump --f5 ssl` captures
* TLS 1.2
* TLS 1.3
* Standard non-F5 captures

Developed and tested on Windows using:
Version 4.7.2 (v4.7.2rc0-29-gac7742f5e15a)

## Notes

This is my first contribution to Wireshark.

The implementation follows an initial discussion about possible approaches with Sake Blok. I would like to thank him for his early review and guidance regarding the overall solution direction.

This work can also be seen as a natural follow-up to the Lua script created by Stig Bjørlykke, extending the concept into native Wireshark support and integrating it with the existing secrets infrastructure.

Feedback and suggestions are very welcome. If there are preferred approaches or coding patterns that would make this change fit better within the Wireshark architecture, I would be happy to adapt the implementation accordingly.

AI-Assisted: yes (chatGPT)

`wsutil/wmem/wmem_strutl.h` defines `ws_memmem`, which calls `memmem` on systems that have it and performs an implementation based on an LGPL 2.1 version of glibc on systems that don't. You could use that, it should be faster.
Thank you for the suggestion. I have updated the code based on your recommendation.

changed this line in [version 3 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25386/diffs?diff_id=1850306898&start_sha=88ad62f7e925e7e11b57acccf64f34bf8dfe917f#f265c78e48b72c96c8cf4c67f0184e3fbea5ae31_42_37)

At first glance, this seems like something that would make more sense to build into wiretap.

Do you have a sample that demonstrates the problem? I would guess that the secrets not being available to be used is quite similar to #20558, where pcapng files are not decrypted on the first pass if the DSB appears too late, but that it works when reloading. Do the F5 secrets similarly work with the existing code if the file is reloaded? I suppose the advantage here is that when the F5 secrets will be used a special packet is included at the start to indicate that secrets will appear later. Such an approach might also be useful for pcapng and DSBs.

That was the first version I made, with wiretap. I ran into the same issue as #20558 <https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/work_items/20558> . Although this situation is a bit different.

A capture made on a F5 BIGP is always a .pcap, not a .pcapng. All the secrets are part of the frames. These are processed after TLS did it’s work, so no decryption takes place. That’s the reason for the current approach.
The advantage we have with a BIGIP capture, is that the first frame is always a special F5 type frame. So we can test at file opening if that frame is present and if it contains “--f5 ssl”. Then we do a prescan for the secrets (before TLS). Otherwise we skip that process.
I attached a small pcap which contains secrets and the special first frame.

[f5-bigip.pcap](/uploads/3b98892e64ef4fbffe87dd8738926812/f5-bigip.pcap)

Thanks, interesting. I guess I would also like to figure out why, unlike with DSBs, redissecting the packets doesn't work. The way that the F5 TLS secrets information is being inserted into the keylog file must be a little different.
Ah, I see, it's because the map gets reset. There's a comment about how it might be nice to separate the map of "keys from the keylog file" from "keys derived at runtime." Hmm.

Interesting. I wasn't aware of that comment. My current implementation simply re-runs the pre-scan when the file is reloaded, so the secrets are populated again. Separating externally supplied keylog secrets from runtime-derived secrets sounds like an interesting future improvement.

Right - we have maps of "secrets that have been read from the keylog file" and of "derived secrets." All of them are reset when a file is reloaded, but the ones read from the keylog file don't really need to be reset; we really don't want to totally re-read the keylog file unnecessarily each time a new file is reloaded or reopened. (We do want to read new entries if it's gotten longer, or re-read it if it's overwritten, etc.)

In your particular file, one problem, as you probably know, is that the same frame has the end of the handshake and also some encrypted extensions that need to be decrypted using the handshake secret. If they were in different frames, a simpler approach would work.

I must admit I never gave that much attention. I was happy enough with a
capture that contains secrets, so I could decrypt the capture. Unfortunately
this is how F5 creates the captures. A pcapng would solve a lot in this
case, and I do want to give a feature request at F5 a try, but I thought
this route would have a greater chance to success.



The first solution I got was kind of an integrated solution of the Lua
script that Stig has made. Upon capture file opening a pms file would be
created and connected to the TLS protocol. That worked. Then Sake mentioned
to find a solution without the need of an extra file. This solution is the
result of that.

Btw, I just removed all changes from packet-f5ethtrailer.c. Those were from
version 1. The file is default again now and not part of the MR anymore.



I do understand the issue with persistency on reload, only my MR was not
meant to be a solution for that. It's only purpose is to remove all manual
work you had to do with tshark/Lua script to be able to decrypt a capture
made on a BIGIP. And I do would like to help solve the issue, but I don't
think I'm the right person for that.
